problem: Learning-based RGB-only image-goal navigation policies struggle to compare goal and observation images when the agent is in a different room from the goal, so they wander or backtrack aimlessly. They lack spatial awareness without depth/GPS.
motivation: Humans first coarsely judge whether they are in the same room as the goal image and leave the room if not. Rooms have characteristic styles (floor, walls, furniture) visible in RGB, so same-room relation may be inferred from RGB alone, but room labels are unavailable and costly.
key_idea: Pre-train a room expert (style encoder + same-room relation network) without labels via constrained clustering (must-link/cannot-link from episode distance), then feed its predicted same-room relation explicitly into an RL navigation policy.
insight: An explicit binary same-room relation is far more useful to the policy than raw room-style embeddings: implicit fusion gets 47.4 SPL / 77.0 SR on Gibson versus 67.1 / 92.9 for explicit fusion (Table ablation of fusion). Room-expert ablation shows both SAM-based data cleaning and constraint-based distance refinement improve same-room accuracy on an MP3D validation set (57.0 -> 58.4), though the gains are small.
method: Room dataset collection: render RGB images from varied angles at start and goal locations of Gibson training episodes, annotated with scene id, episode id and difficulty (easy/medium/hard); blank images are removed with SAM mask-count threshold.

Constraint matrix M: cannot-link (-1) for different scenes, must-link (1) for same location, 0.5 for same easy episode, -0.5 for same hard episode; used to refine feature distance D - gamma*M (adaptive gamma).
Unsupervised clustering: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50 style encoder, InfoMap clustering on refined distances gives pseudo labels, trained with cluster-level contrastive loss.
Room relation network: takes concatenated style embeddings of two images and predicts same-room or not with cross-entropy; total loss L_cluster + omega*L_pred (omega=1).
Navigation policy: FGPrompt-EF style, ResNet-9 encoder on channel-concatenated observation and goal (6 channels), 2-layer GRU policy trained with RL (distance/angle reward, success reward).
Explicit fusion: frozen room expert outputs a 2-d relation flag concatenated with visual feature as policy input; implicit fusion instead fuses style embeddings E_s(I_t), E_s(I_g).

setting.backbone: ResNet-9 visual encoder + 2-layer GRU policy (RL, trained from scratch) with frozen room expert (ResNet-50 style encoder + relation net)
setting.training_data: Gibson training episodes (72 scenes) for RL for 500M steps; room expert pre-trained on self-collected unlabeled Gibson-rendered images (no external data)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30°, STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT distance only used in training rewards and room-expert constraints from episode difficulty)

numbers.extra: averaged over 3 seeds; 500 max steps, 1 m success

numbers_note: Split names for cross-domain sets are not explicitly stated; 'test' is assumed. Implicit-fusion variant numbers are in the fusion ablation (Gibson 47.4/77.0, MP3D 33.2/59.9, HM3D 27.7/55.8).
results: REGNav reaches 67.1 SPL / 92.9 SR on Gibson, beating FGPrompt-EF (66.5/90.4), and beats memory-based methods (MemoNav, TSGM) on Gibson hard (59.4 SPL / 87.1 SR vs 57.9/74.7 for MemoNav). Cross-domain it gets 50.2/78.0 on MP3D and 44.0/75.2 on HM3D versus FGPrompt-EF 48.8/75.7 and 42.1/75.2.
limitations: Gains over FGPrompt-EF are modest, especially in cross-domain SR (HM3D SR tied at 75.2), and the room expert accuracy is only about 58% on MP3D.
Room labels are heuristic (distance-based difficulty), noisy, and depend on Gibson episode structure; the expert is not evaluated on the navigation-relevant relation beyond same/different room.
